attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: 'Will wind up' is firm, unhedged language with an open 'sooner or later' horizon. The proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: The plain reading treats a capable general-purpose system as powerful AI, criminal or abusive actors as bad hands, and usable access as being in their hands. That is ordinary and not stretched. The surrounding text also hints at military or corporate hands, but the narrower criminal reading is fair.

evidence.note: Anthropic's primary incident report, available Nov 2025, before the evaluation date. It describes attackers using Claude Code in Sept 2025 for reconnaissance, exploit writing, credential theft and data exfiltration. It is a company disclosure and not independently verified, but it is the kind of primary record the contract allows.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met by a dated event after publication. Anthropic's incident report describes malicious actors who jailbroke Claude Code and used it for intrusions and data theft in Sept 2025. The report is a company disclosure, and the packet notes that independent scrutiny of the telemetry was not obtained. Even so, it is a detailed primary incident record of actual misuse, not a hypothetical demonstration, so it meets the contract's source requirement.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: In context, 'all about money' attributes Google's change to its weapons and surveillance principles to financial pressure. That is a causal claim about motive.

contract.note: Reading 'all about money' as a dominant financial motive, not the only one, is fair to the speaker. Asking for decision records or corroborated testimony is reasonable for a claim about motive.

evidence.note: Google's own blog post of Feb 4, 2025 gives geopolitical and national-security reasons for the change. This is the stated rationale only. It neither proves nor rules out a dominant financial motive.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is Google's public explanation, which cites global competition and national security. A company's stated rationale cannot establish or exclude its real motive. No internal records or participant testimony were found linking financial pressure to the decision, so the evidence does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Presumably' hedges only the premise, that Google is not yet making zillions from AI. 'Cannot continue indefinitely' is firm, with no deadline. The drafter keeps the hedge on the premise and treats the second clause as a forecast.

contract.note: Requiring the premise to be established first, reading 'making money' as returns after costs, and treating the forecast as open-ended are all fair. The contract adds no deadline or threshold the speaker did not give.

evidence.note: Alphabet's Q4 2025 call reports enterprise AI generating billions in quarterly revenue and higher Cloud operating income. These are revenue and segment figures, not AI returns after all attributable costs, and they do not show the 2024 premise.
Google's Q3 2026 CEO remarks, dated the evaluation date, report 103% Cloud growth driven by AI and continuing capacity expansion. This shows neither an end to the effort nor isolated net AI returns.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and the evidence does not meet the early-resolution rule. The disclosures show large AI-driven revenue and Cloud profit, but not AI returns after costs, and not an end to the investment. The hedged premise about Google's position in early 2025 is also not established. A finite period cannot contradict this forecast, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Reading between the lines' marks how Marcus reached the view, but the assertion that the effort is not paying off is firm. It is correctly treated as an observation about the position at the end of Q4 2024.

contract.note: Reading 'paying off' as financial benefit in proportion to AI investment and costs, anchored to Q4 2024, is an ordinary plain reading. It is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: In the Q4 2024 call, the CFO cites AI monetization momentum and billions in annual Cloud AI revenue. That is revenue, not return after costs, though it weakens the inference Marcus drew from the call's silence.

The Q4 2024 earnings release shows that shared AI R&D costs, including general model development, are kept outside segment results. Segment profit therefore cannot show the all-in return on AI investment.

reviews.rationale: No evidence in the packet isolates Google's AI-specific returns against its AI costs for the period up to Q4 2024. The revenue statements are gross figures, and the segment data leaves out shared AI costs, so the evidence neither supports nor contradicts the claim that the effort had not yet paid off.
